S40.01.note: Opening Settings from the account menu relies on AccountMenuItems.tsx using the Settings label; the account menu trigger's own visible text was not confirmed. Onboarding also asks Preferred name (OnboardingWizard.tsx) but this item is the Settings path.
steps: Sign in, open the account menu and choose Settings, then choose Personalization.
Scroll to About you and type a nickname in the field with the placeholder Nickname or first name.
Wait for the save status to show Saved, then start a new chat and ask a question.
Check that the reply uses that name, as in Expected.
S40.01.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > What should AGI call you?

steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to About you and type background in More about you, for example interests or your situation.
Wait for Saved, then start a new chat and ask a question that needs the background.
Check that the reply takes the background into account, as in Expected.
S40.02.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > More about you

S40.03.note: The role choices come from WORK_DESCRIPTIONS in a constants file; the list's visible text was not read.
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to About you and open the What best describes your work? menu.
Pick a role from the list, wait for Saved, then ask a question in a new chat.
Check that the reply is pitched at that role, as in Expected.
S40.03.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > What best describes your work?

S40.05.note: The same choice is also in Settings > Personalization > Style and tone > Response style.
steps: In a chat, click the Style control in the composer.
Under Response Style, pick Concise, Explanatory, Learning or Formal (or Default).
Send a question and look at the reply shape.
Check that the reply follows the chosen style and only one style is active, as in Expected.

S40.06.note: Settings > Personalization > Response length uses other labels (Default, Shorter, Longer), so the two controls are not the same list.
steps: In a chat, click the Style control in the composer.
Under Response Length, pick Brief, then send a question.
Pick Thorough, send the same question, and compare the lengths.
Check that the reply length changes with the choice, as in Expected.
S40.06.where: Composer > Style > Response Length (Brief, Default, Thorough)

S40.07.note: Settings > Personalization > Style and tone > Response style also lists Formal.
steps: In a chat, click the Style control in the composer.
Pick Formal under Response Style.
Send a casual question and read the reply.
Check that the wording is formal, as in Expected.

S40.08.note: The code has no separate tone control; the named presets are the only tone choice found.
steps: In a chat, click the Style control in the composer.
Pick one preset under Response Style, for example Concise.
Send a question and compare the reply with the Expected tone.
Switch to a different preset, send again, and check that the reply changes.
S40.08.where: Composer > Style > Response Style (Default, Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal)

steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open Warmth.
Pick More, then ask a question in a new chat.
Check that the reply is warmer, and repeat with Less to compare, as in Expected.
Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open Enthusiasm.
Pick More, then ask a question in a new chat.
Check that the reply is more enthusiastic, and repeat with Less to compare, as in Expected.

S40.11.note: Preferred formatting (Not set, Prose, Bullet lists, and others) is a second control for the same idea.
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open Headers and lists.
Pick Less, ask a question in a new chat, then pick More and ask again.
Check that the first reply is prose and the second uses headers and bullets, as in Expected.
S40.11.where: Settings > Personalization > Characteristics > Headers and lists

steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open Emoji.
Pick Less, ask a question in a new chat, then pick More and ask again.
Check that emoji appear only on the More reply, as in Expected.
Open Settings, then Personalization.
Under Style and tone, open Technical level and pick Beginner.
Ask a technical question in a new chat.
Check that the reply is explained for a beginner, then pick Expert and compare, as in Expected.
S40.13.where: Settings > Personalization > Style and tone > Technical level

S40.14.note: This is separate from Display Language in General, whose label is in apps/web/features/settings/sections/GeneralSection.tsx.
steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Under Style and tone, open Response language and pick a language other than Match my message.
Send a message in English in a new chat.
Check that the reply is written in the chosen language, as in Expected.
S40.14.where: Settings > Personalization > Style and tone > Response language

steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Type standing instructions in the Instructions for AGI box and wait for Saved.
Start a new chat and ask a question that the instruction should change.
Turn off the switch labelled Apply instructions for AGI, ask again in a new chat, and compare, as in Expected.

S40.17.note: The sidebar menu item that opens Project settings was not confirmed by its visible text; the dialog title was used instead.
steps: In the sidebar, open a project's menu and choose Project settings.
Type text in the Instructions box and click Save.
Open a chat inside that project and ask a question.
Check that the reply follows the project instructions, as in Expected.
S40.17.where: Sidebar > Projects > project row menu > Project settings > Instructions

S40.19.note: The per-chat scope was read from the code, not tested.
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and pick a style such as Concise.
Send a question in this chat and check the reply is short.
Open a second chat and leave its style at Default.
Check that the second chat keeps its own style and the Settings default is unchanged, as in Expected.

S40.20.needs: a sample of your own writing (paste text)
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and choose Create Custom Style.
Type a Name, paste text into Writing sample, and click Save.
Select the new style and ask for a short piece of writing.
Check that the reply matches the voice of the sample, as in Expected.
S40.20.where: Composer > Style > Create Custom Style > Writing sample

steps: Open Settings, then Personalization.
Change Response style and a few Characteristics.
Click Reset response style and read the toast.
Check that the controls return to Default and the toast says Response style is back to the defaults, as in Expected.
In a chat, click the Style control and pick Explanatory under Response Style.
Ask how a simple process works.
Check that the reply gives reasoning and context, as in Expected.
In a chat, click the Style control and pick Learning under Response Style.
Ask a question about a topic you want to learn.
Check that the reply goes step by step with check-ins, as in Expected.
In a chat, click the Style control and pick Concise under Response Style.
Ask a question that normally gets a long answer.
Check that the reply is short and direct, as in Expected.

S40.27.note: The Edit and Delete controls use aria labels Edit {name} and Delete {name}; the confirmation says the style cannot be recovered.
steps: In a chat, click the Style control and choose Create Custom Style.
Enter a Name and a Style instruction, then click Save. Use the Edit control on the style to change it and Save changes.
Select the style, ask a question, and check the reply follows it.
Use the Delete control, read the confirmation and choose Delete style, then check the style is gone, as in Expected.
S40.27.where: Composer > Style > Create Custom Style (edit with the pencil, delete with the trash icon)

labels.text: Use your profile and instructions for AGI

S40.30.needs: a project and a saved personal instruction
S40.30.note: The sidebar menu item that opens Project settings was not confirmed by its visible text.
steps: Open a project's Project settings from its sidebar menu.
Under Personalization, check or uncheck Use your profile and instructions for AGI.
Click Save, open a chat in that project, and ask a question.
Check that the reply uses your personal instructions only when the box is checked, as in Expected.
S40.30.where: Sidebar > Projects > project row menu > Project settings > Personalization
